headline: Old Harbor Has a Ghost — and It Leaves Case Files
body:
Seven bodies have been recovered from the flooded ruins of Old Harbor over the past four months, each bearing the same signature: partial submersion, BCI hardware surgically extracted post-mortem, and a laminated index card left in a sealed bag on the victim's chest containing what Metro Homicide is describing only as 'structured personal data.' Metro Homicide's Organized Crime liaison confirmed the case file designation OM-2127-044 exists, but declined all further comment. The victims range in age from 23 to 61 and have no apparent connection to one another by employment, corponation affiliation, or district of residence. 'Whoever this is, they're not sloppy,' says a source within the Graycloaks who asked not to be identified. 'The BCI extractions are clean. Clinical. This person knows the hardware.'

Old Harbor's geography makes it a nightmare for conventional law enforcement — the 2089 sea wall failure left the district a maze of half-submerged buildings, unstable walkways, and flooded transit tunnels that metro drones cannot reliably navigate. The Bore Rats, who maintain the most extensive network of routes through the area, say they have seen 'someone who doesn't belong' moving through the deeper channels on three separate occasions but have declined to bring the information to official authorities. Community advocates note that three of the seven victims were synthetics, raising unresolved questions about whether Metro Homicide is treating those cases with equal investigative priority.

A self-described urban archaeologist named Cassiel Huang-Owusu, who has operated an unauthorized salvage business in Old Harbor for eleven years, says the index cards are the detail that haunts her. 'They're not trophies in the normal sense. They're organized. Like someone is keeping records on people, and when the record is complete, they decide the person is done.' Metro Homicide has not confirmed the content of the cards. A spokesperson for Axiom's private security division confirmed that one victim, Matteo Solis-Park, was a former Axiom contractor, but declined to characterize his role.
aftermath: By 2129, the body count attributed to the Old Harbor case — designated the 'Index Killer' in underground media — had reached fourteen, with no arrest and Metro Homicide reassigning the case lead twice under unexplained circumstances.
runner_relevance: The Index Killer case became one of the most lucrative and dangerous runner-adjacent situations in the 2120s. Graycloaks offered escalating bounties for intelligence on the killer's identity or the content of the index cards — starting at 4,000 quanta and reaching 22,000 quanta by 2128. Axiom quietly hired runners for a parallel investigation into Solis-Park's death that they kept separate from Metro Homicide, offering 9,000 quanta for evidence retrieval from his Old Harbor access points. Victims' families and synthetic rights groups hired runner investigators at personal rates. The Bore Rats began offering paid guide contracts specifically for parties moving through Old Harbor kill-zones, knowing the premium clients would pay. At least two known runners disappeared while working the case.
